events.title: Afternoon walk — Rue Saint-Honoré to Stohrer via Les Halles
events.note: Party of 3 · 90 min · Rue Saint-Honoré east → left at Rue du Pont Neuf → Allée André Breton through Les Halles gardens → Rue Montorgueil north to Stohrer10 things to look out for, in order:1.La Samaritaine— Approaching Rue du Pont Neuf, look right: the LVMH-restored Art Nouveau landmark, closed 15 years and reopened 20212.Bourse de Commerce — Pinault Collection— The round 16th-century grain exchange dome visible off Rue de Viarmes, now a contemporary art museum3.Fontaine des Innocents(Place Joachim-du-Bellay) — As you enter Les Halles: Paris's oldest surviving monumental fountain, carved in 15494.Forum des Halles Canopy— The sweeping glass-and-steel roof over the subterranean complex; peer down into it as you cross above5.Jardin Nelson-Mandela— The garden above the Forum where Allée André Breton runs; lively square with locals at lunch6.Église Saint-Eustache— The north face rises dramatically off the garden: Flamboyant Gothic exterior with Renaissance interior, one of the largest churches in Paris7.Rue Montorgueil market stalls— The pedestrian street opens with fruit vendors, cheese shops, and flower sellers; watch for La Fermette (cheese) and Palais du Fruit8.L'Escargot Montorgueil(#38) — Look up for the giant gilded snail above the door; restaurant founded 1832, still serves escargot, foie gras and oysters9.Fou de Pâtisserie(#45) — Paris's first pastry concept shop: rotating creations from the city's top pastry chefs all in one window10.Stohrer(#51) — The oldest patisserie in Paris, founded 1730 by Louis XV's personal pastry chef; famous for its baba au rhum and the original Art Nouveau painted ceiling insideAlso very nearby:G. Detou(58 Rue Tiquetonne — specialty grocery, baking ingredients & hard-to-find pantry goods) ·A. Simon Paris(48 Rue Montmartre — professional kitchenware since 1884) ·MORA(13 Rue Montmartre — pastry & baking equipment) ·E. Dehillerin(18 Rue Coquillière — legendary copper cookware, open since 1820)

events.title: The Louvre
events.note: Party of 3 · 3 hours · Tickets already purchased — no changes or cancellations · Nearest métro: Palais Royal – Musée du Louvre (lines 1, 7)Arrival:Arrive by 9:15 AM and look for a staff member holding a “9:30 AM” sign. Enter through thePorte des Lionsentrance. If no one is at that entrance, head straight down into the undergroundCarrousel du Louvreentrance instead — accessible via the street at 99 Rue de Rivoli or directly from the Palais Royal–Musée du Louvre métro station.Step-by-Step Route to the Mona Lisa:1.Clear Security & Enter— Walk through the Porte des Lions gate and pass through the security checkpoint.2.Take the Stairs— Immediately after scanning your ticket, take the stairs or elevator up to the 1st Floor (Level 1 in Europe) of the Denon Wing.3.Walk Through the Spanish Galleries— You will emerge into the Spanish and Italian painting galleries. Walk straight down the long corridor (Grand Galerie), moving eastward toward the centre of the museum.4.Turn Right at Room 711— Look for the massive wide entrance on your right-hand side leading into Room 711 (Salle des États).5.Behold the Mona Lisa— She is located on the large freestanding wall directly across from Véronèse’s massive painting,The Wedding Feast at Cana.
events.address: Rue de Rivoli, 75001 Paris, France

events.title: Walk — St. James's Park (Guards Memorial to Buckingham Palace)
events.note: Route: start at the Guards Memorial · head into the park and pick up the lake's north bank path (better morning light, closer to the water than the Mall-side path) · pause at the Blue Bridge — the single best vantage point on the lake, with views both ways · continue west along the north bank toward Duck Island at the lake's west end, the park's main bird sanctuary and the best spot for pelicans, herons, and the resident waterfowl · exit the park at the west end and walk up to Buckingham Palace. Early morning (park opens 5am) means fewer crowds and more active birds — look for the famous pelicans, plus herons, cormorants, coots, moorhens, and tufted ducks along the way.
events.address: From Horse Guards Road, London SW1A 2AX, United Kingdom To Buckingham Palace, Buckingham Gate, London SW1A 1AA, United Kingdom
